input.quote: 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
input.rationale: The Services licence in 13.1 is granted to Customer alone, expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors, is non-transferable, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — squarely in walk-away territory on affiliate/contractor exclusion. Sections 13.2 and 13.3 only partially cure it: 13.2's perpetual, irrevocable Affiliate- and contractor-enabled grant is limited to paid-up software and Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables, not the subscription Services, and while 13.3 provides successor/Affiliate transfer and limits revocation to uncured material breach after notice (which meets the fallback on those two points), it gives no path for Affiliates or contractors to use the Services themselves. Redline extends the 13.1 grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and ties revocation and transfer to 13.3.

proposal.summary: Extend the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove revocation at Vendor's discretion
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Services licence in 13.1 to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and removed revocation at Vendor's sole discretion so that revocation is governed by the uncured material breach standard already agreed in 13.3. Our playbook requires affiliate and contractor coverage and no at-will revocation; if helpful, we can instead cover Affiliates on written notice to Vendor.

ops.oldText: Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
ops.newText: Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf, a licence to use the Services, transferable as provided in Section 13.3 and revocable or suspendable only as provided in Section 13.3.
